title: George Cumby Joins the College Football Hall of Fame Class of 2026
question: Which Oklahoma Sooner was selected for the College Football Hall of Fame in 2026?
answer: Linebacker George Cumby (OU 1975-79) was named to the College Football Hall of Fame's 2026 class, becoming the 25th former Oklahoma player chosen. His induction is scheduled for Dec. 8, 2026, in Las Vegas.
summary: OU linebacker George Cumby made the College Football Hall of Fame's 2026 class as the 25th Sooner player chosen. Here are his stats, honors and NFL career.
body: The National Football Foundation added another Sooner to college football's most exclusive roster in January 2026, naming linebacker George Cumby to its 2026 College Football Hall of Fame class. He becomes the 25th former Oklahoma player selected, and his induction is set for the 68th NFF Annual Awards Dinner on Dec. 8, 2026, in Las Vegas.

Cumby's OU career (1975-79) began in the backfield. As a redshirt freshman fullback he scored a rushing touchdown in the 41-7 Fiesta Bowl win over Wyoming after the 1976 season. Moved to linebacker before 1977, he took off: Big Eight Defensive Newcomer of the Year in 1977, Big Eight Defensive Player of the Year in 1978 and 1979, a first-team AP All-American in 1977 and a unanimous All-American in 1979.

The numbers still stand out. His 437 career tackles rank second in school history, including 160 in 1979. He made five interceptions in 1978, tied for the most ever by an OU linebacker in a season, and his 32 career bowl tackles remain a school record. As a starter he went 32-4 with four Big Eight titles.

Green Bay took Cumby in the first round of the 1980 NFL Draft, and he played eight pro seasons with the Packers, Bills and Eagles, earning second-team All-Pro honors in 1982. Afterward he coached and became an ordained minister.

His selection continues a defensive streak for Oklahoma. The five Sooners chosen just before him were also defenders: Rod Shoate (2013), Brian Bosworth (2015), Rickey Dixon (2019), Roy Williams (2022) and Dewey Selmon (2024).
